content.text:
I found only one CPRD code that specifically means eosinophilic oesophagitis.

## Codelist: Eosinophilic oesophagitis

| Read code | Term |
|:----------|:-----|
| J1017 | Eosinophilic oesophagitis |

**What I searched**
- **By term:** "eosinophilic oesophagitis", "eosinophilic esophagitis", "eosinophil", "esophag eosin", "allergic oesophagitis", "eosinophilic gastro" and "EoE". Every search that found anything returned only J1017 for this condition.
- **By code:** everything under J101 (oesophagitis). J1017 is the only code there for eosinophilic oesophagitis.

**Codes I left out on purpose**
- **General oesophagitis codes** (J101 Oesophagitis, J101y Other specified oesophagitis, J101z Oesophagitis NOS): these don't say what kind of oesophagitis it is.
- **General eosinophilia codes** (D403 Eosinophilic disorder, D403z Disorder characterised by eosinophilia, D4033 Allergic eosinophilia, D4035 Hypereosinophilic syndrome): these don't point to the oesophagus.
- **Raised eosinophil count** (42K3): this is a blood test result, not a diagnosis.

Because there is only one code, you could also look at prescriptions (such as budesonide orodispersible tablets) or endoscopy and biopsy records to find more cases. Those are outside this diagnosis codelist.

content.text:
I found only one CPRD code for eosinophilic oesophagitis:

| Read code | Term |
|:--|:--|
| J1017 | Eosinophilic oesophagitis |

**How I searched**
- **By term:** "eosinophilic oes", "eosinophilic es", "eosinophil", "oesophagitis", "allergic oesoph" and "eosinophilic gastr". J1017 was the only code for this condition, and there were no other wordings of it.
- **By code:** "J1017" has no sub-codes under it.

**Codes I left out**
- **Other types of oesophagitis** (J101, J101y, J101z and the J1011 reflux codes): these are broader or different diagnoses.
- **Body-wide eosinophilia codes** (D403 and its sub-codes, such as hypereosinophilic syndrome): these don't point to oesophagitis.
- **Eosinophil count test codes** (42K, 42K3).

Because there's only one code, this list will only find patients whose condition was recorded specifically as eosinophilic oesophagitis. Some may have been coded as "Oesophagitis NOS" (J101z) or "Other specified oesophagitis" (J101y), especially before the diagnosis was widely recognised. If you'd rather catch more patients at the cost of some wrong matches, you could add those codes, ideally with a second check such as a prescription of swallowed budesonide or fluticasone.
